title: The finish line
kind: a build chapter: the feedback window, the saved score and the banner
one: You build the feedback window that shows how every summit went. Save my score puts the score on the Top 10, and a banner on the Welcome window says what it means.

stages.title: See what happens at the finish line

screens.title: Look at the feedback window and the banner

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know what the player sees from the last summit to the Top 10.
An expedition ends when all 8 summits are climbed, or when the player clicks **Finish the expedition**. Then the feedback window opens.

screenshot.alt: The feedback window, with the total at the top, the 8 summits down the left, and the feedback for one summit on the right
screenshot.cap: The feedback window that you build in this chapter.

blocks.p: The total is at the top, out of 800 points. Down the left is a [[ListBox|0]] with one line for each summit and its score.
Clicking a summit shows its feedback on the right: the score, a bar that fills to match it, what went well and what went wrong.
**Save my score** saves the score to the scores file. The map closes, and the Welcome window shows again.
Straight after a save, a gold banner shows on the Welcome window, above the Top 10. It shows only once, and it says one of 4 things.
**Case A:** the player was not on the Top 10 before, and now is. The heading says **You made the Top 10!**
**Case B:** the player was on the Top 10, and this is a new best score. The heading says **New best score!**
**Case C:** the player is still on the Top 10, but this score is not their best. The heading says **Still in the Top 10**.
**Case D:** the player is not on the Top 10. The heading says **Expedition saved**, and the message says the score needed to get on.
In cases A, B and C, the player's row on the board is highlighted. You typed that in chapter 7.

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know that your project has everything the finish line needs.
The finish line uses the map, the practice game and the Welcome window, so check each one first.

need: Your project, with the practice game opening from the map (chapter 9).
The Welcome window, with the gold banner, ShowBanner and MoveBoard (chapter 7).
ScoreFile, with Save, BestScore, PlaceOf and TenthPlaceScore (chapter 7).
About 2 hours. Your ticks are kept, so you can stop at the end of any screen and come back later.

words: A box that shows a list of lines. The player clicks a line to pick it.
The number of the line picked in a ListBox, from 0. It is -1 when no line is picked.
A bar that fills from left to right. Its Value says how full it is, from 0 to 100.
Adds words to the end of what a TextBox already shows.
Runs the lines inside it once for each item in a list.
One single character, such as a letter. A char goes in single quotes, such as `'A'`.
blocks.intro: You do not need to learn these words now. Where you first meet each one in the chapter, it has a dotted line under it. Hover over it or tap it to see what it means.

screens.title: Add the banner fields, and work out which case it is

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, Expedition remembers the save, and can work out which of the 4 cases it is.
The feedback window saves the score, but the Welcome window shows the banner. So the facts the banner needs go in Expedition, where every window can read them.

code.title: The banner fields
partLines: The save
`JustSaved` turns true when a score is saved, so the banner shows once. `LastSavedScore` is the score that was saved.
Before the save
The player's best score and place before this save. -1 means no score yet, and place 0 means not on the board.

code.title: BannerMessage
code.why: The first 4 lines get the facts the message needs. The copy gives you those lines and case D. You type cases A, B and C, which change with the player's place.
partLines: The facts
The player's name, their place now, the place in words such as 3rd, and the sentence about the highlighted row.
Case A
The score, and the place it puts the player in.
Case B
`move` says **moves you up to**, unless the place is the same as before. Then it says **keeps you**.
Case C
This score, then the best score, which is what keeps the player on the board.
Case D
`TenthPlaceScore` from chapter 7 gives the score to beat to get on the board.

code.title: A new heading for case A
task: Find the line for case A in BannerHeading, in Expedition.cs.
Change its words to `Welcome to the Top 10!`
code.test: Register a new player, then finish and save an expedition with that player.
code.expect: The banner heading says **Welcome to the Top 10!**
code.hint: A new player is not on the board before the save, so the save is case A while the board has fewer than 10 players.

blocks.p: When the test passes, put the heading back to **You made the Top 10!**

screens.title: Check that the finish line works

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you know every part of the finish line works, including refusing to close without saving.

Run each test with F5. Tick each test when it passes. A test marked "Must be refused" should do nothing, and that counts as a pass. Log in as `peakBagger`, with the password `tick800`, for these tests. A new player is not on the Top 10 yet, so no row of theirs could be highlighted.

check.what: Finish with 1 summit climbed, then click **Yes**.
check.how: The feedback window opens with the title **Expedition finished early**.
check.fix: Check the first `if` in frmFeedback_Load, then check that frmFeedback_Load is in the box beside **Load** in the Properties window.

check.what: Click a summit that was not climbed.
check.how: The white box says **You did not climb this summit, so it scored 0.** and the bar is hidden.

check.what: Click the X on the feedback window, then click **No**.
check.how: The feedback window stays open. Nothing is saved.
check.fix: Check frmFeedback_FormClosing, then check that it is in the box beside **FormClosing** in the Properties window.

check.how: The map closes. The Welcome window shows the banner, and your row on the Top 10 is highlighted.
check.fix: Check btnSave_Click, OpenFeedback in frmMap.cs and ShowBanner in frmWelcome.cs.

check.what: Click **Start the expedition**, then **Back to the welcome screen**.
check.how: The banner has gone, because it shows only once after each save.

blocks.p: Take a screenshot of each test as it passes. Press the Windows key, Shift and S together, then drag a box around the part of the screen to keep.
Paste each screenshot into your testing document, under the test it shows.

glossary: A box that shows a list of lines. The player clicks a line to pick it.
The number of the line picked in a ListBox, from 0. It is -1 when no line is picked.
A bar that fills from left to right. Its Value says how full it is, from 0 to 100.
Adds words to the end of what a TextBox already shows.
Runs the lines inside it once for each item in a list.
One single character, such as a letter. A char goes in single quotes, such as `'A'`.
